mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL level above 250 predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to inflation fears compressing real equity valuations and increasing risk aversion.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 250, the 20-day forward returns are non-negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.5%, it signals monetary tightening that increases real rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, the 20-day forward returns are non-negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) by more than 0.2pp and fall in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% over 3 months signals an impending recession, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and INDPRO falls > 0.5% over 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are non-negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and rising for 3 months), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to increased real rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and rising for 3 months), the 20-day forward returns are non-negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A HOUST level above 1200 (thousands of units) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to strong housing market signaling robust economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1200, the 20-day forward returns are non-positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it signals an overheating economy that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5%, the 20-day forward returns are non-negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of more than 0.25% signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.25% in the last month
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month, the 5-day forward returns are non-negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of real GDP (GDPC1) exceeds 2.5%, it predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to strong economic growth supporting corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 year-over-year growth rate > 2.5%, the 60-day forward returns are non-positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
